notes.title: The First Feature Vote - Results are in!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! 
Stephen here bringing you the first big news updated post launch. We've spent this entire month working on bugs, and as we wrap up august, we're starting to look at adding new features…..

AND YOU DECIDED!
[h1]A creature that pulls from chests.[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35579864/f0ffffbfdfa98eb1d5438639b116c5e60d130c54.png[/img]

Let's talk about this. We've been watching a ton of playthroughs, the steam forums, and the discord, and it's apparent that our automation system isn't where we need to be. 

This is a larger fundamental issue about what we want Atrio to be. When we started the project, we had decided that we couldn't possibly reach the depth and complexity of Factorio or Satisfactory, and very early on all agreed that we would go for a "simpler" automation approach. It should be a little easier to get a base up and running, the level of complexity to beat the game would be less, and refactoring a base wouldn't be nearly as daunting. I mean, you already have so much to deal with (power, the dark, finding items, head explosions….).
At this point, automating something like power is SUCH a pain.

[h2] We'll be rethinking what it means to automate in Atrio[/h2]
starting with the Factory.
Currently, in order to set up a good factory line, you either need individual assembly lines, or a ton of pushback splitters - but capturing and combat is a mid-late game experience.
Setting up satisfying factory lines doesn’t come in until much later. 

[h2]How are we going to tackle this? [/h2]
Short answer…. We don't know, but here's our first idea. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35579864/dc687b549e9608818e76419b899ea78c8a49d533.png[/img]

Each of the factories pull from the assembly line when they need resources. This would greatly simplify the process, and the pushback splitters would actually be used as splitters, not as inserters.

[h2][h1]Ok, but the creature that pulls from chests?[/h1][/h2]
[i]Option 1: [/i]I found a note from 2019 that I should make a creature called the grab-crab. No promises, but maybe I'll explore the grab-crab. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35579864/1741eb1e5993a4e61b56136d88b69d9ab874b861.jpg[/img]
[i]figure 1. a very serious and pretty much totally definitely real in game screen shot of the grab crab.[/i]

[i]Option 2: [/i]To be more inline with making automation easier, We may even forgo having a grab, and just make a chest that automatically dispenses items.

The results just came in so I need more time to explore the different ideas.

[h1]Language support.... bad news[/h1]
Bad news here....we need to sell more copies of the game to justify localizing into another language. Atrio hasn't sold enough for us to afford more localization. It was a bit of a lofty goal on our part, but I wanted Atrio to be accessible to everyone around the globe. Hopefully we'll continue to see great community engagement, and sales so we can have the budget to pay for great localization.


[h1]This month has been all about bug fixes[/h1]
We close out our month of bug-fixing Sept 1, and it's on to our first real month of feature work :)
SEE YOU SOON!

-Stephen,
Isto inc.

notes.title: Minecraft pleasures meet a gorgeously automated dystopia in Atrio: The Dark Wild
notes.notes:
There's something very "Steam game" about Atrio: The Dark Wild. I don't know exactly what a Steam game is but if you think of Steam as pistons and valves, the colour black, and that ultra-low thunk of a piano key when a Valve logo pops up on the opening screen of some classic, I think it's that. Atrio is dark, literally and figuratively. It has some of that lovely, satisfying kind of automated crafting. It's a bit political, and a bit funny, in its own way, the game you giggle at villainously from your racing car throne in some enjoyably dingy, PC monitor-lit bedroom. So: Steam game, whatever that is.

In Atrio you play as an android with a 15-minute battery. Your task is to do what you're told, popping out of a tube onto the overworld, which is desolate and grim but also remarkably stylish. Atrio is a stunner, a kind of isometric plane of geometric art, the natural world rebuilt, presumably - this is far-future dystopia, of a sort - as if it were some utilitarian cuckoo-clock. Seemingly mechanical deer skip about, eating sap and pooping out fuel. The ground is littered with things like blood ore and quartz and little flowers with rosy, glowing cuboid bulbs that power a nearby generator, which powers lightbulbs, which connect to more machinery that enables more research to build more, and onwards.

Light is central to all of this. You start in a fairly small area, without light and with just that generator nearby - stray into the nearby dark and, within a few seconds, you'll die. The bulbs of those little flowers offer a little, temporary power to light the nearby ground but not much, and so one of your early tasks is to make fuel that can top the generator up to max in one go. That requires blood rock, which you turn into blood ore, which you turn into blood ingots, which combine with some other bits and bobs to make the batteries for the generator. All of these tasks come from a central computer, which has a fondness for exploding your head when you're done and firing up a new android to take your place.

notes.title: This genre-bender is a creepy marriage of Factorio and Don't Starve
notes.notes: In Atrio: The Dark Wild you're an android in an abandoned, neon cyber city. Everything is dark, the city is filled with rogue, vicious cyborg animals, and you need to get the lights back on. It's an open world survival crafting game fused with an automation-factory building game. Also, because it's about horrible dog-things with pusher plates for heads pouncing out of the darkness to murder you, you're likely to get spooked at least once... Read more.

notes.title: Atrio's First Public Playtest - June 11- June 13
notes.notes:
[b]IMPORTANT: You MUST opt-in to the playtest on our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1125390/Atrio_The_Dark_Wild/]steam page[/url] BEFORE June 11, 5pm MST.[/b]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/JThw2T6.png[/img]
We will be letting everyone who has opted in to play! 


[b]Atrio's First Public Playtest[/b]

We are trying to create the satisfying, and absurd assembly line to use in our upcoming trailer, and we need your help!  The top  submission is going to win a free copy of the game on launch!

In creative mode, you have unlimited resources, but only a few types of items. Your goal is to create a gif showing off your assembly line in 30 seconds or less.


[b]Details: [/b]
You can use any program you want, I personally use OBS since its free and easy to use.
You can also use the windows game bar, by pressing windows G

If you don’t have a computer that's good enough to record gifs, 
Join our  [url=https://discord.gg/BBByZfQ]discord[/url] and you can send a screenshot. If the screenshot is nutty, we'll try to make it work.

After you record a gif, upload it to twitter and tag us. If you don't have [url=https://twitter.com/istoinc?lang=en]twitter[/url], join our [url=https://discord.gg/BBByZfQ]discord[/url] and send it there.  

We're going to be ranking them purely on satisfaction, so get ready to make some JUICY gifs :)

-Stephen, Isto inc.

notes.title: Beta test this weekend! (Now Over)
notes.notes:
We will be randomly picking 200 lucky users to playtest our game this weekend!! 

[b]How to enter:[/b]
Go to our Steam Page and click "Request Access" [img]https://i.imgur.com/JThw2T6.png[/img]
(if you've already clicked the button, you're all good!)

[b]When to sign up?[/b]
Sign up BEFORE Friday, March 26 @ 5pm MST 

[b]When is the playtest?[/b]
Friday, March 26 @ 5pm MST -> Monday, March 29 @ 10am MST

[b]How will I know if I've been picked?[/b]
All the winners will get an email at around 5pm MST on Friday notifying them that they have access to the playtest, and Steam should automatically activate it in your library!

[b]Will you run more tests?[/b]
Heck ya we will! Expect more a bunch more playtests in the future


-Stephen
